newsitem.title: TURKEY: Amnesty pushes for meeting with Turkey's Erbakan.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty pushes for meeting with Turkey's Erbakan.

text.p: The head of Amnesty International is to visit Turkey this week in the hope of holding talks with Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on the country's human rights record, the rights group said on Tuesday.

Amnesty has written and telephoned the Turkish embassy in London to try to arrange a meeting between secretary general Pierre Sane and Islamist Erbakan on Friday, Amnesty spokeswoman Anita Thiessen said.
"So far they have not said yes and not said no," she told Reuters. "At some point they are going to have to give an answer."
The European Parliament criticised Turkey's human rights performance last week.
Sane, due in Turkey on Thursday, also hopes to meet Islamist Justice Minister Sevket Kazan and right-wing Interior Minister Mehmet Agar.

The European Parliament, angered by what it sees as Turkey's reneging on promises to improve human rights and its failure to help end the division of Cyprus, threatened last week to block hundreds of millions of dollars of European Union aid to Ankara.
The EU was due to give Turkey 375 million Ecus ($470 million) by the year 2000 to help it adapt to a customs union that went into force in January.
